title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this 'Analysis situs' draft (1986), Grothendieck builds a combinatorial, tame-topology theory of 'figures' and 'préfigures'. These are finite cellular structures, here worked out in dimension one, on an ordered line L. M_1 denotes the set of closed segments of L. A 'drapeau' D = (X_1 <| X_2 <| ... <| X_n) in Drap*(M_1) is a finite chain of segments, each lying entirely to the left of the next. They are therefore pairwise disjoint.

This page states a structure proposition: an arbitrary 1-dimensional préfigure is determined by the following data.

(1) A figure Ψ without isolated vertices whose connected components are segments. Equivalently δΨ = ∂Φ, so the 'combinatorial boundary' equals the topological boundary of the underlying set. Such a Ψ is Φ_D, the disjoint union of the segments X_i of a flag D. Its boundary ∂Ψ = δΨ is the disjoint union of the endpoint pairs ∂X_i = {a_i, b_i}. So Ψ is equivalently encoded by a strictly increasing sequence of even length, a_1 < b_1 < a_2 < b_2 < ... < a_n < b_n, with X_i = S_{a_i,b_i}.

(2) Postponed to the next page.

(3) A finite ordered set of points Δ in Drap*(L) with Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ. From it one deduces a partition (finished on p.115) Δ = ∂Ψ ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ Δ_is:
- Δ_int = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ) consists of the points lying inside the open intervals ]a_i, b_i[.
- Δ_is consists of the remaining points, which are isolated.

Further data (p.115):
- A subset Δ_lac ⊂ Δ_int of 'lacunary' vertices (holes), with Δ_red = Δ_int \ Δ_lac the 'redundant' (subdivision) vertices.
- A subset ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ of 'proper boundary' vertices, i.e. endpoints that actually belong to the set.

The préfigure is then recovered as follows:
- P_0 = ∂_0 ∪ Δ_red ∪ Δ_is.
- P_1 = the interstitial open intervals of Δ contained in the shadow Omb(Ψ).

In modern terms, this is the classification of finite cell decompositions (stratifications into points and open intervals) of constructible / semi-linear subsets of the line. The data are:
- the closure, a finite union of disjoint segments plus isolated points;
- a finite vertex set refining the boundary;
- which interior vertices are deleted (holes) and which are kept (subdivision points);
- which endpoints are included.

It serves the program of describing 'tame' spaces combinatorially by dévissage from dimension one.
errors: No substantive error. The struck-out word 'strictement' is in fact needed: since the segments are disjoint and non-degenerate one needs a_i < b_i < a_{i+1}. The strict symbols '<' in the displayed chain already encode this.
The case n = 0 (empty Ψ, all points isolated) is implicitly allowed but not mentioned.
The proposition is stated before all the data are listed: item 2°) is deferred and the partition of Δ is completed on the next page. It is a draft, not a finished statement.

ideas.what: Encoding a finite disjoint union of closed segments on a line by a flag of segments, or equivalently by a strictly increasing sequence of even length of endpoints.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary combinatorial description of compact semi-linear subsets of R (o-minimal / tame topology in dimension 1).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s).
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), not worked out there.

ideas.what: Classification of a 1-dimensional 'préfigure' (a cellular structure that is not necessarily closed) by: closure figure Ψ, vertex set Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ, lacunary vertices Δ_lac ⊂ Δ_int, and proper boundary vertices ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ.
ideas.modern_name: Cell decompositions of constructible subsets of the line; locally closed / partial CW-type structures; stratified sets with distinguished strata.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (cell decomposition theorem in o-minimal geometry for dimension 1).
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Montpellier notes (cote 156-8).

ideas.what: Terminology distinguishing vertices: isolated, interior, lacunary (holes), redundant (subdivision), and proper boundary. Combinatorial boundary δ versus topological boundary ∂, and the 'ombre' (shadow/support) Omb.
ideas.modern_name: Strata types in a stratification; frontier condition; support/closure.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); terminology here is Grothendieck's own.

missed.claim: This is a documented piece of Grothendieck's actual working-out (1986) of the 'tame topology' program announced in Esquisse d'un programme. It begins a combinatorial classification of préfigures from dimension one. The mathematics is elementary, but the specific formalism (figures/préfigures, flags Drap*, ombre, lacunary/redundant vertices) is not in the literature.
missed.quote: Proposition Une préfigure quelconque est déterminée par les données suivantes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for reconstructing how Grothendieck intended to found tame topology combinatorially. There is no new mathematical result for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary combinatorial classification of 1-dimensional cell structures on a line. It is a draft step in an unpublished tame-topology program and contains nothing a specialist would find mathematically novel.
transcription_corrections: In 'Ψ = Φ_D = ⋃_{X∈D} X̃_ξ' the subscript ξ is doubtful. Most likely just X̃ (or a stray mark) is meant, giving ⋃_{X∈D} X̃ = ⋃_{1≤i≤n} X̃_i.
'2°) ici, cf. p. 10 suivante' is more plausibly '2°) ici, cf. p. suivante' (refer to the next page).
The insertion reads 'sans sommets isolés et, à composantes connexes des segments (i.e. telle que δΨ = ∂Φ)'. The 'i.e. δΨ = ∂Φ' is written once under the phrase and repeated as a gloss.
